---
title: Pandoc blank-line rules
---

A heading needs a blank line before it in Pandoc:
# Not a heading, text of the paragraph above

Same for a block quote:
> Not a quote.

and for a list:
- not a list item
- still the same paragraph

and for an ordered list:
1. neither is this

With the blank line they are what they look like:

# A heading

> A quote.

- an item
- another item

1. one
2. two

Inside a list item the next marker still starts an item, and nesting works:

- outer
  - nested
- next
  1. nested ordered
  2. second

A line after a list item that is not a marker is part of the item:

- item text
# not a heading either
> nor a quote

Known difference: Pandoc keeps these two lines in the quote as lazy text, here they end it:

> a quote
# lazy line, not a heading
- lazy line, not an item

> A nested quote needs its blank `>` line
>
> > like this

Things that still end a paragraph:

text before a fence
```python
print("fenced")
```

An underlined line is a setext heading
==========================================

#5 is not a heading in Pandoc either, nor is #hashtag.
